Spiced Advent Tea

Served at: Second Sunday of Advent

Serves 4-6Prep 5 minCook 10-15 min

This comforting Spiced Advent Tea is a perfect beverage to warm your soul and home during the Second Sunday of Advent. As the days grow shorter and the anticipation of Christmas builds, a fragrant cup of this tea offers a moment of peaceful reflection and brings the festive aromas of the season indoors.

Ingredients

  • 6 cups (1.4 L) water
  • 4 black tea bags (or 4 teaspoons loose leaf black tea)
  • 2 cinnamon sticks
  • 1 teaspoon whole cloves
  • 2-3 star anise pods (optional)
  • 1 inch (2.5 cm) fresh ginger, thinly sliced
  • Peel from 1/2 an orange (use a vegetable peeler to get wide strips, avoid white pith)
  • Honey or sugar, to taste (optional)
  • Orange slices or extra cinnamon sticks, for garnish (optional)

Method

  1. In a medium saucepan, combine the water, cinnamon sticks, whole cloves, star anise (if using), sliced ginger, and orange peel.
  2. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat.
  3. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer gently for 5-7 minutes to allow the spices to infuse.
  4. Remove the saucepan from the heat. Add the black tea bags (or loose leaf tea in an infuser) to the spiced water.
  5. Cover and let steep for 3-5 minutes, or to your desired strength. Be careful not to oversteep, as black tea can become bitter.
  6. Remove the tea bags or infuser and strain the tea through a fine-mesh sieve into a teapot or heatproof pitcher to remove the spices.
  7. Serve hot, sweetening with honey or sugar to taste, if desired.
  8. Garnish each cup with an orange slice or an extra cinnamon stick, if you wish.

Tips

  • For a stronger spice flavor, gently crush the cloves and cinnamon sticks slightly before adding them to the water.
  • You can make a larger batch of the spiced water ahead of time and store it in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently and add fresh tea when ready to serve.
  • Experiment with other spices like cardamom pods or a pinch of nutmeg for a different flavor profile.
